 Crime Hyderabad ED searches seven premises over alleged ₹326.4 crore bank fraud
 Harsha Vardhini 23 Oct 2026 4:59 PM Share this: HYDERABAD: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at seven premises in Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Medchal-Malkajgiri on October 23, 2026, in connection with an alleged ₹326.49 crore bank fraud involving Kanakadhara Ventures Pvt. Ltd. (KVPL).
 The ED’s Hyderabad Zonal Office carried out the searches under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. The premises included the company’s registered office, the residences of its directors and locations linked to entities and individuals suspected of facilitating the diversion of bank funds. 
 The investigation concerns the alleged diversion of credit facilities sanctioned to KVPL and its directors.

 CBI registered case on Punjab National Bank complaint
 The ED initiated its investigation based on FIR No. RC0782022E0005, dated December 8, 2022. The Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) Banking, Securities and Fraud Branch (BS&FB), Bengaluru, registered the case following a complaint by Punjab National Bank (PNB).
 The FIR alleges offences under Sections 120-B, 420, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The allegations concern KVPL, its directors and others. 
 Bank consortium alleges loss of ₹326.49 crore
 According to the ED, the case involves the alleged defrauding of a consortium of banks led by PNB. The other lenders were IDBI Bank, Union Bank of India, Andhra Bank (now part of Union Bank of India) and Bank of Baroda. The alleged loss to the consortium amounts to ₹326.49 crore.
 The investigation has found that bank guarantee and letter of credit facilities sanctioned to KVPL were allegedly misused. Funds were reportedly diverted through related entities and intermediaries, using fabricated steel purchase invoices and transport documents.
 The ED has also found that KVPL operated bank accounts outside the consortium arrangement without the lending banks’ knowledge.
 During the searches, officials found and seized documents, digital devices and other records allegedly linked to the diversion and layering of funds. The ED has also identified multiple immovable properties and investments.
 Further investigation is under way.
